title: Pilot cohort anchor and unstick cheatsheet
content:
Context and intent:
This is a personal working note for running small pilot cohorts with an explicit 'anchor' tenant and an unstick strategy for when traffic or quality drifts. Not a ship doc — think of it as the pragmatic checklist I run through before booking an escorted pilot. Focus: minimize blast radius, keep client happy, and ensure easy remediation if model/infra noise shows up.

High-level goals:
- Verify warmup behavior for KV/cache priming across real clients (small but noisy queries).
- Confirm that routing + pinning semantics are reversible with no visible client churn.
- Exercise telemetry and the three-tier rollback ladder (soft pin -> siphon -> hard rollback).
- Validate that dedicated warmup cohorts actually reduce p95 tail within first 10 minutes.

Constraints and assumptions:
- Pilot size: 0.5%–2% of global traffic (target depends on client SLA and backlog).
- Window: prefer low-traffic region windows first (UTC 02:00–06:00).
- Anchor tenant: single landlord/enterprise that agrees to be the first warmed tenant; they receive an 'escort' (Slack + weekly check-ins).
- We assume autoscaling for model variant is enabled; burst capacity not relied on.

Definitions (how I use terms here):
- Anchor: chosen tenant we intentionally route more of the pilot traffic to for priming and observation.
- Unstick: sequence of actions to recover a tenant that shows increasing error/latency or quality regression.
- Escort window: a 2–6 hour period where SEs/Oncall/AE are on-call for the tenant.

Pilot sequencing (preferred order):
1) Dry-run in staging with recorded traffic for this tenant (full replay of top 200 queries). 
2) Canary 0.1% with anchor pinned to new variant (15m baseline).
3) Ramp anchor to 1% over 30m if no signals.
4) Open a second warm cohort (0.5% mixed customers) to validate cross-tenant interactions.
5) Shift anchor back to baseline if any unresolved alerts or client-facing regressions.

Warmup tactics (anchor-specific):
- Prefix pre-warm: send 5–10 synthetic requests representing heavy KV usage immediately after pin.
- Token budget: allow up to 2x normal token consumption for anchor during first 20 minutes to build KV cache.
- Localized cache seeding: issue prioritized sample requests (top 50) to warm embeddings/kv.

Traffic shaping heuristic (practical numbers I use):
- Ramp schedule: 0.1% -> 0.5% -> 1% over 45m with 3 hold checkpoints (15m each).
- Abort on signal if any of the following persist for two consecutive check windows:
  * p95 latency increase > 35% vs baseline AND absolute p95 > 1200ms
  * error-rate (5xx) > 0.3% sustained
  * hallucination regression metric (eval set) drops > 4 points
- If minor blips (single-window spike), wait one stabilization window and run quick checks (latency heatmap + CPU/GPU util).

Unstick ladder (ordered escalation):
1) Soft-pinback: reduce the cohort fraction for affected tenants by 50% and remove concurrent new cohorts.
2) Siphon buckets: move 30–50% of traffic to a compatibility model variant with lower latency but similar quality.
3) Tenant-escort immediate: notify AE/SE, open a parallel log stream, and run targeted priming.
4) Hard rollback: flip anchor tenant to previous model version (requires 3 approvals for tenants with SLAs).

Escape hatches (fastest mitigation):
- Edge throttle (per-tenant) — kill additional concurrent requests for that tenant; quick and least invasive.
- SDK-level client toggle — if client has a toggle we can ask them to flip temporarily.
- Regional diversion — if problem isolated by region, divert traffic to alternate region (watch for cold cache downstream).

Observability and checks (what I look at first):
- Latency by route and by tenant (p50/p95/p99), with absolute numbers and % change.
- Error classification: client (4xx) vs server/runtime (5xx) vs model-quality flags.
- Token cost delta and request path (did caching reduce tokens?).
- KV hit-rate for anchor tenant over time (goal: >60% within 20m).
- Model output SNR for anchor eval subset (quick sampling automation).

Dry-run checklist (do these before any live cohorts):
- [ ] Replay top-200 tenant queries in staging and confirm KV warming patterns.
- [ ] Create a staging metric dashboard that matches prod panels.
- [ ] Set temporary alerts with shorter windows (3/5m) for the pilot.
- [ ] Coordinate Escort Slack channel and recipient list.
- [ ] Confirm rollout toggle and pin commands exist and are tested.

Client communication snippet (starter for emails/Slack):
"Hi <client>, launching a short pilot window tomorrow 02:00–06:00 UTC. We'll prime your tenant and monitor latency/quality closely. You'll have a private channel with our team and we can roll back instantly if anything looks off. Expected impact: transient higher token usage for 10–20 mins while we warm caches. Let me know if that conflicts with your peak windows"

Simulation notes (outputs I care about):
- Staging replay: median warming time 8m (goal < 12m), KV hit-rate reaches 65% at 12m.
- Synthetic load: p95 uplift of 18% during warmup but returns within 2 windows.

Open questions / TODOs for follow-up:
- Can we add a temporary per-tenant token cap to prevent runaway token consumption in warmup? (JIRA ticket suggested)
- Need an automated 'anchor snapshot' that captures trace + top-100 prompts at pin time for faster RCA.
- Confirm whether regional diversion triggers cold-start billing alerts for customers (billing implications).
- Align with AE playbook for larger enterprise anchors (approval flows).

Quick references (tickets to check during pilot):
- JIRA-RINF-6123: anchor-tenant-approval-flow
- confluence:pilot-cohort-anchors-2026 (design notes and previous runs)
- PR #1347: routing toggle improvements (adds per-tenant siphon)

Notes to self (utterly informal):
- If anchor is chat-heavy, expect slower initial p95 due to context window; add extra priming messages.
- Keep the first warm cohort under 30 minutes if it's my first time with that client.
- Consider running two overlapping anchor windows (different days) for clients with strict SLAs so we can compare warmups.

End of scratchpad. Will tidy and extract into a small runbook if the next two pilots behave well.
